summary: ```markdown # Marvelous Designer Outline Tutorial ## Introduction Hello everyone! In this video, we will explore the **name line function** in Marvelous Designer. This feature allows you to create items such as necklaces and sewing line effects. Let's dive into how to add and modify outline properties and customize outline types. ## Adding a Name Line To begin, locate the tool group for the name line in the **2D window**. Click on the **Edit Name Line Tool**. You will see a small scissors icon; click on it to reveal the entire menu. ### Editing Existing Name Lines The first tool in the menu is used for editing name lines that have already been created. Let's first learn how to add a new name line. When using the **Line Section Name Line function**, it operates similarly to the Line Division function. By selecting the Line Section Name Line Tool, your mouse will hover over the line section. It uses the straight line point as the basis to identify each line section. 1. Click on a line section. 2. In the **3D window**, you will see that the name line has been added. 3. In the **2D window**, a plum red highlight indicates that the name line has been created. 4. The name line will automatically be added to the symmetrical version. You can click on other lines to add additional name lines. It’s essential to note that even if these lines are related, the name lines created using the Line Section Name Line function are not linked automatically. ### Deleting Name Lines If you need to delete any excess name lines, use the **Edit Name Line function** to select the name line and press the delete key. Alternatively, right-click while selecting a name line and choose "Delete" from the output menu. ## Using the Free Name Line Tool Now, let’s take a look at the **Free Name Line Tool**. This tool allows you to freely choose the starting and end points of a name line. 1. Click on the starting point. 2. Move your mouse to create the name line. 3. Click on the endpoint. ### Effects of Creating a Free Name Line When you create a free name line, the entire line is connected, which means it naturally connects at the corners. If you wish to delete these lines, you can do so as needed. ## Exploring the Powder Line Tool Next, let’s discuss the **Powder Line Tool**. This tool creates a line along the powder line. 1. When you switch to this tool, all powder lines will be marked. 2. As your mouse moves over a line with a powder line, a corresponding point at the other end will move together. The operation method of this tool is similar to the Free Powder Line, but it automatically follows the powder line. ### Creating a Powder Line To create a powder line: 1. Click the starting point. 2. Move your mouse to the desired position and click the endpoint. You will see in the **3D window** that along this group of powder lines, there are powder lines on both sides. ## Editing Powder Lines Let’s discuss some operations that can be performed with the **Edit Powder Line Tool**. 1. **Adjusting End Points**: To adjust the endpoint of a powder line, select it, click the endpoint, and drag it to the desired position. You can also drag the middle of the line to move the whole line. 2. **Selecting All with Same Attributes**: Right-clicking on a powder line in the menu bar allows you to select all lines with the same attribute. The selected powder lines will be displayed in a high saturation plum red. 3. **Applying New Powder Line Types**: After selecting this option, a new powder line type will be added, applying this default type to the selected powder lines. 4. **Adding Inner Lines**: Choosing this option will automatically create an inner line that follows the current position of the powder line. ### Editing Attributes After selecting a powder line, you can adjust its attributes in the **Attribute Editor**. Here, you can modify the name of the powder line, apply different powder line types, or adjust the extension settings. ## Corner Settings Let’s take a look at corner settings. 1. **Curve Option**: Selecting this option will create a curve instead of a sharp angle at the corner. You can set the length of the curve. 2. **Right Angle Corner**: This option only works on powder lines at the outer corner. It automatically generates a 90-degree corner. 3. **Distance Between Corners**: This is the distance between powder lines. Smaller numbers bring lines closer together, while larger numbers push them further apart. 4. **Turn Option**: When selecting the turn, the powder line will automatically turn to the other side of this line. ## Fabric and Outline Specifications Now, click on the name of the fabric window, find the **Top Stitch** in the drop-down menu, and switch to the line type. In the property editor, you can adjust various properties, including: - **Offset**: Controls the gap between lines. - **Name Line Type**: The name line type can be just a sticker or a real 3D grid. ### Customizing Your Own Name Line Type To define your own single loop name line type, return to the name line table and add a new name line type. Choose the appropriate OBJ file for your design. After adjusting the length and thickness of the name line, you may need to increase the interval to ensure the design displays correctly. ## Adjusting Physical Properties After setting up the design, you might encounter issues with stretching and deformation. To resolve these: 1. Reduce the strength of the fabric properties to make it easier to stretch. 2. Increase the bending strength to avoid small wrinkles and deformation. Once the simulation is opened, you will notice an improvement in the effects. ## Troubleshooting Custom OBJ Patterns Sometimes, using your own OBJ pattern may lead to surface issues due to unit differences. Ensure that the OBJ pattern aligns with the units used in Marvelous Designer. Adjust the ratio in the property editor and ensure the size is correct for proper alignment. ## Conclusion In this tutorial, we covered how to effectively use the name line and powder line functions in Marvelous Designer, including adding, modifying, and deleting lines, as well as creating custom line types. Thank you for watching, and see you in the next video! ```
